success_patterns: Write the quantifiers in each option in their actual scope before comparing them; in particular, determine whether a witness is chosen once for all targets or may depend on each target.
For two-sided asymptotic bounds, compare the lower- and upper-bound scales in the stated limiting regime; a reversed asymptotic ordering cannot be repaired by changing fixed positive constants.
When asked for an exact general classification, check the full scope of the claim, including both directions of an iff and whether it applies to every parameter choice or only a restricted subclass.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers quantifier scope, equivalences, and exact parameter ranges. A useful addition from this batch is a quick internal consistency check for simultaneous asymptotic lower and upper bounds, which can eliminate options whose scales are ordered impossibly.

edits.content: - For simultaneous asymptotic lower and upper bounds, compare their scales in the stated limit before selecting an option. If the proposed lower-bound scale eventually exceeds the upper-bound scale, no fixed positive constants can make both inequalities hold uniformly.
